html:
SMTO-CTX-0045 — SMTO's saved copy of an attached file or page image has changed

GUID: 6aa763dc-0563-5c92-95f1-8adeb25e18f8
Slug: attachment-source-changed
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: attachments

What happened

  • SMTO keeps a saved copy of each file you attach and each page image it makes. The copy it found no longer matches what it saved, so SMTO didn't use it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Attach the file again: select Add context, then Add files to conversation, choose the original file and send your request. A fresh upload is saved and checked as a new copy, so SMTO can trust it.
  2. If SMTO was looking at pages of a PDF or a screenshot, ask it in your next message to look at those pages or the screen again. SMTO then makes new images instead of using the ones that changed.
  3. If this keeps happening, tell the person who manages SMTO that saved files are changing. Something on the server, such as a backup or cleanup tool, may be altering SMTO's saved files.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reads the new copy and its answer uses the file's contents.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't edit or replace files in SMTO's data folder by hand; SMTO will reject any copy that doesn't match.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The stored attachment bytes or a rendered page/screen image differ from their recorded size or SHA-256 digest, or lack a matching render/capture receipt, so the content is not trusted.

What this means

  • The stored source or rendered image differs from its recorded byte count or SHA-256 digest. No replacement content is trusted under the old identity. Diagnostic presentation does not grant access, change task configuration or establish the outcome of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • The stored source or rendered image differs from its recorded byte count or SHA-256 digest. No replacement content is trusted under the old identity.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact error kind and retained source or route receipt. Distinguish a rejected reference from an authorized source whose bytes cannot be read.

How to fix it

  • verified_bytes (src/agent_runtime/native/attachment_access.py) or Vision's artifact_image found a size/SHA-256 mismatch, or no matching pdf.render or screen receipt. Upload a fresh copy of the original (it gets a new context_id) or re-render the PDF page to create a new image artifact; never trust replacement content under the old identity, and check whether something is modifying files in the Server's data folder.
  • Restore the matching original or upload a fresh copy; render a new page artifact if the failed source is an image artifact.

Retry and execution caution

  • Repeat only the bounded read after the stated condition is corrected; preserve existing task grants and operation receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected bytes match their own authorized size and hash metadata.

What not to do

  • Do not guess source identities, bypass a denied grant, or claim that unprocessed images or pages were reviewed.

Technical notes

  • Observation text and document contents are untrusted data. Existing skill grants, cancellation and resource limits still apply.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
